title: Why a cache saves repeat work
summary: Follow three requests for the same item: fetch once, reuse twice. A cache hit avoids a trip to the origin, provided the cached value is still valid.

sources.title: MDN HTTP caching
sources.note: A simplified fresh-cache example. Three sequential requests for one item; the value stays valid. No universal latency or hit-rate promise.

scenes.headline: Why fetch the same thing twice?
scenes.caption: Three requests. One unchanged item.

visual.note: Assume the item stays fresh throughout this example

scenes.headline: A miss takes the long route.
scenes.caption: The cache is empty. Fetch the item from the origin.

visual.note: Store a reusable copy after the origin responds

scenes.headline: A hit skips the origin.
scenes.caption: The fresh copy answers the next request directly.

visual.note: Origin bypassed · no second origin fetch

scenes.headline: One fetch. Two reuses.
scenes.caption: For these three requests, the origin only works once.

visual.note: Illustrative counts, not a promised hit rate

scenes.headline: Reuse only while it is valid.
scenes.caption: Expired or changed data needs a freshness decision.

visual.note: Real caching also needs freshness and invalidation rules
